source_context:
298:     state: absent
   299:   loop:
   300:     - shared
   301:     - pipeline
   302: 
   303: - name: Extract package source on server
   304:   ansible.builtin.unarchive:
   305:     src: /tmp/lamware-pkg-src.tar.gz
   306:     dest: "{{ pipeline_install_dir }}/pkg/"
   307:     remote_src: true
   308:     owner: pipeline
   309:     group: lamware
   310: 
   311: - name: Ensure staged package source is traversable by the lamware group
   312:   # Both the pipeline venv (owner) and the api venv (group lamware) install
   313:   # from this tree. Symbolic +X grants execute (traverse) on directories only,
   314:   # leaving files non-executable. Idempotent on already-deployed hosts, unlike
   315:   # copy's directory_mode (which only touches newly created dirs).
   316:   ansible.builtin.file:
   317:     path: "{{ pipeline_install_dir }}/pkg"
   318:     state: directory
   319:     owner: pipeline
   320:     group: lamware
   321:     mode: "u=rwX,g=rX,o="
   322:     recurse: true
   323: 
   324: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   325: # Pipeline virtualenv — the host-side orchestrator (run-pipeline.py), report
   326: # generator, and wrapper DB-failure handler run from this venv, so the
   327: # pipeline runtime no longer depends on --break-system-packages.
   328: #
   329: # The `pipeline` user is iptables-network-locked (cannot reach PyPI), so:
   330: #   * the venv is created as the pipeline user (offline — bundled ensurepip)
   331: #   * a wheelhouse is built as ROOT (root is not network-locked, and building
   332: #     on the host guarantees correct platform/python3.12 wheels)
   333: #   * all installs run as the pipeline user, offline, from that wheelhouse
   334: # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   335: 
   336: - name: Ensure python3-venv is installed (for the pipeline virtualenv)
   337:   ansible.builtin.apt:
   338:     name: python3-venv
   339:     state: present
   340: 
   341: - name: Create the pipeline virtualenv (offline; bundled ensurepip)
   342:   ansible.builtin.command:
   343:     cmd: python3 -m venv "{{ pipeline_install_dir }}/venv"
   344:     creates: "{{ pipeline_install_dir }}/venv/bin/pip"
   345:   become: true
   346:   become_user: pipeline
   347: 
   348: - name: Create the pipeline wheelhouse directory
   349:   ansible.builtin.file:
   350:     path: "{{ pipeline_install_dir }}/wheelhouse"
   351:     state: directory
   352:     owner: pipeline
   353:     group: lamware
   354:     mode: "0750"
   355: 
   356: - name: Check whether the wheelhouse already holds wheels
   357:   ansible.builtin.find:
   358:     paths: "{{ pipeline_install_dir }}/wheelhouse"
   359:     patterns: "*.whl"
   360:   register: pipeline_wheelhouse_existing
   361: 
   362: - name: Populate the wheelhouse as root (reaches PyPI; the pipeline user cannot)
   363:   # Building on the host guarantees wheels match the host platform + python3.12.
   364:   # Includes pip/setuptools/wheel because py3.12 venvs omit setuptools, and the
   365:   # offline source-builds of the lamware packages need a build backend.
   366:   ansible.builtin.command:
   367:     cmd: >
   368:       python3 -m pip download
   369:       --dest {{ pipeline_install_dir }}/wheelhouse
   370:       pip setuptools wheel
   371:       requests weasyprint markdown psycopg2-binary pydantic
   372:       ppdeep==20260221
   373:   register: pipeline_wheelhouse
   374:   changed_when: "'Saved' in pipeline_wheelhouse.stdout"
   375:   when: pipeline_wheelhouse_existing.matched | int == 0
   376: 
   377: - name: Make the wheelhouse readable by the pipeline user
   378:   # The populate step runs as ROOT (the pipeline user is network-locked), and on
   379:   # a hardened host root's umask leaves the downloaded wheels 0600 root:root —
   380:   # unreadable by the become_user: pipeline installs that follow. Hand ownership
   381:   # to pipeline:lamware and grant traverse/read (symbolic +X = dirs only). Runs
   382:   # UNCONDITIONALLY (not gated on the populate `when`) so a wheelhouse left
   383:   # root-owned by an earlier failed run self-heals on the next converge.

     5:   ansible.builtin.apt:

     7:       # steamcmd is a 32-bit binary; these provide its runtime without needing a full
     8:       # i386 architecture on the host.

    13:     state: present
    14:     update_cache: true
    15:     cache_valid_time: 3600
    16: 
    17: # Deliberately the tarball rather than the `steamcmd` apt package. That package is i386-only,
    18: # so installing it means `dpkg --add-architecture i386` — a system-wide change that doubles apt
    19: # metadata and invites i386 library sprawl on a host that otherwise has none, all for one test
    20: # rig. (Multiverse is already enabled on ubuntu-cube; the package still has no candidate purely
    21: # because no foreign architecture is registered.) The tarball is self-contained and needs only
    22: # the 32-bit runtime above.
    23: - name: Create the steamcmd directory
    24:   tags: rust-test
    25:   become: true
    26:   ansible.builtin.file:
    27:     path: "{{ rust_test_server_steamcmd_dir }}"
    28:     state: directory
    29:     mode: '0755'
    30:     owner: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"
    31:     group: "{{ rust_test_server_user }}"

    39:     dest: "{{ rust_test_server_steamcmd_dir }}"
    40:     remote_src: true
    41:     creates: "{{ rust_test_server_steamcmd_dir }}/steamcmd.sh"
    42: 
    43: # Owned by the panel's SSH user directly, rather than the group-membership dance the
    44: # containerised servers need (compscidr/iac#486). The panel writes here to snapshot,
    45: # rewrite the seed and delete map files; owning the tree outright is the simplest way
    46: # to grant that, and this host runs nothing else that needs the directory.
    47: - name: Create the server directory

    50:   ansible.builtin.file:

    60: # thing it manages. `app_update` is a no-op when already current, so running it every

    62: - name: Install or update the Rust dedicated server

   291:       # argv avoids all shell quoting: the script is passed intact, base as $1.
   292:       # A ~8GB ISO takes a few minutes of IO — hence the generous async window.
   293:       # rc != 0 (e.g. PREFLIGHT_FAIL, exit 3) fails the task with the stderr shown.
   294:       ansible.builtin.command:
   295:         argv:
   296:           - docker
   297:           - run
   298:           - --rm
   299:           - --pull=missing
   300:           - -v
   301:           - "{{ _dst_dir }}:/isos"
